headline: Two held in Nurzhan over fake Bazar heater and air-filter ads; 14 buyers lost 5,900 som
dek: Police say advances of 120 to 600 som were sent by card transfer outside the Tulpar app as smog and the heating season set in.
paragraphs: Nurzhan City Police detained two men on 3 November on suspicion of fraud after 14 residents paid advances for space heaters and room air filters that were never delivered. The detainees are a 27-year-old Nurzhan resident, born 1999 (D.K.), and a 31-year-old from Neftegorodok, born 1995 (R.S.).

Capt. Yelena Gavrilyuk, the city police press officer, said the listings appeared on the Bazar board in the Tulpar app at low prices as the heating season began. Buyers were asked to send an advance by Talasbank card transfer outside the app, on the promise that a courier would deliver. Advances ranged from 120 to 600 som, about 5,900 som in all. Officers seized a number of SIM cards and a laptop.
The offers came as Nurzhan's air worsened. The air quality index reached 216, rated very unhealthy, on 4 November, with district heating on and a temperature inversion over the city.

Azamat Joldoshbekov, Tulpar's head of trust and safety, said the listings had been removed. "Bazar deals are arranged in chat and paid in person," he said, and users should treat any request to pay in advance by transfer as a warning sign.
Captain Gavrilyuk said the case file is with the prosecutor, who will decide on the charge. No court date has been set, and the men are presumed innocent until a court rules.
